description: Four initial contextual findings resolved by the explicitly approved fresh-on-view policy. This does not certify the rest of the Spanish corpus or authorize publication.

issues.finding: The two occurrences describe feathers inside the pillow, not writing instruments.
issues.proposedAction: Review an explicit correction to the feather sense and all three questions; decide how prior practice of the incorrect gloss should affect existing mastery. Do not silently transfer mastery to another sense.
issues.resolution: Both occurrences now reference sns_es_pluma_feather. Retain old pens sense, questions, and progress as history; no progress transfer.

issues.finding: The Palma occurrence ultimátum médico is adjectival; the Quiroga occurrences denote a doctor. The current single sense conflates the two uses.
issues.proposedAction: Prepare separate noun/adjective analyses and quiz sets. Decide the mapping of the old ambiguous mastery identity explicitly; do not copy its mastery to both new senses.
issues.resolution: Palma adjective uses sns_es_medico_medical and a separate adjective surface/lemma. Both Quiroga doctor occurrences retain the original mastery key. New adjective mastery begins on view only.

issues.finding: In mirando a su mujer the contextual meaning is his wife, not merely an unspecified woman.
issues.proposedAction: Review the spouse sense and implications for the existing generic quiz/mastery identity before adoption.
issues.resolution: The spouse occurrence now uses sns_es_mujer_spouse. Retain the old general-woman sense, questions, and progress; do not transfer it.

issues.finding: In paso por esa funda the form functions as a verb in a construction expressing acceptance; it should not be combined with the noun pasos meaning footsteps.
issues.proposedAction: Review pasar and the construction in context, prepare its proper questions, and decide the old mastery mapping explicitly.
issues.resolution: The occurrence uses sns_es_pasar_accept under a new pasar verb lemma and first-person present surface. Old step history and separate plural pasos noun remain untouched.
